formex v7 plan — read_*/write_* verbs and a two-axis leaf

Source: ONTOLOGY-V7-PLAN.md

Scope + design note, 2026-10-26. Responds to datagoodr/dev/formex-devnote-schema-simplification.md (asks 2, 3, 4) and to the proposal to split format_label into a unit axis and a style axis. The quick fixes from that note (the as_yyyy/as_ein recipe bugs, the stale CSV) are already landed; this note is the larger, not-yet-implemented work.

1. Three operations, not one

Today one verb per ontology row (raw_to_stable_transform = {{ as_mmddyyyy }}) bakes the parse and the canonical output into a single step, so formex can only ever emit the canonical/ISO form. Decompose it into three composable pieces:

verb direction example notes
read_<style> written form → canonical internal value read_mmddyyyy("03/15/2019") → a Date this is today’s as_*, the parse half
write_<style> canonical value → a chosen written form write_yyyymmdd(date) → "2019-03-15" the new half
convert_<unit→unit> canonical value in one unit → another unit convert_C_F(20) → 68 changes meaning, not rendering

A full stabilizer composes them:

{{ read_mmddyyyy :: write_yyyymmdd }}                 # re-render, same unit
{{ read_celsius  :: convert_C_F :: write_1dp }}       # unit change + render

write_* normalizes first, then renders (per the datagoodr note): internally write_X(v) = render_X(canonicalize(v)), where canonicalize is the read_*/ as_* recast. So write_* is safe to call on already-stable or raw-ish input — it idempotently re-reads before writing. That keeps read_* :: write_* robust even when the caller hands it a half-cleaned value.

Mapping to the current code. read_* aliases the existing verb table in R/20-fx-stabilize.R (as_mmddyyyy, as_email, as_ein, …); datagoodr already renamed its ingest verbs as_* → read_*, so the vocabularies line up. write_* is net-new: a small renderer per format_style (below). convert_* is a third, smaller registry keyed on (from_unit, to_unit) — most units have no converter and that is fine (the pair is simply unavailable).

2. The leaf is two axes: format_style and unit_type

format_label today is mostly a copy of semantic_type (calendar/calendar, usd/usd, email/email) and only occasionally does real work (range/{comma_pair,to_range}, coordinate/{dms,iso6709}). The proposal — a good one — is to replace it with two orthogonal sub-axes so a variant is a combination rather than an enumerated leaf:

  • format_style — the written rendering that determines parse and render but not meaning: date field-order and separators (the mask together), currency suffix-scaling ($12b), abbreviated-vs-full (CA vs California), comma-pair vs lo to hi. This is what read_*/write_* key on. Usually value-detectable.
  • unit_type — the dimensional or categorical unit that carries meaning and may need a convert_* or is metadata-gated: USD/EUR, C/F, fiscal-vs-calendar year, measurement unit (kg/m), geographic level (state/county/country). Often not value-detectable, so frequently NA.

A variant = (semantic_type, format_style?, unit_type?), either sub-axis optional. Define a variant only as far as it affects parsing — if a type has one style and no meaningful unit, both are NA and the leaf is the semantic_type. Depth 4 is reached when either sub-axis resolves; resolving format_style alone is still depth 4 even if unit_type stays NA (datagoodr renders that as an empty unit facet).

Settled: order lives in format_style

Date field-order (mmddyyyy vs ddmmyyyy vs yyyymmdd) and separators both live in format_style — together they are the mask the parser needs, and order is a parse parameter, not a unit of measure (the unit of a calendar date is always day-of-month-of-year). unit_type is reserved for a genuine dimensional/categorical unit where a convert_* or a metadata gate is meaningful. This keeps “resolve the unit” meaning one coherent thing in every family, and it is the axis datagoodr asked to surface resolved on $route (their ask 3), so the two converge on the same field.

Worked mapping

path today format_label → format_style unit_type
temporal/date/calendar calendar mdy_slash · ymd_dash · mdy_smash —
temporal/period/year year bare · FYyyyy calendar · fiscal
number/currency usd / euro / balance plain · grouped · suffix_scaled · accounting USD · EUR
number/quantity/measurement measurement plain kg · m · C · F … (metadata)
text/name/place place abbreviated · full state · county · country
number/range/min_max comma_pair / to_range comma_pair · to_range · bracketed —

This collapses the usd/euro/balance and comma_pair/to_range enumerations into one semantic_type row crossed with the two small, controlled vocabularies, and kills the format_label == semantic_type redundancy across most of the 96 rows. The detector’s job becomes: match the semantic_type, then resolve any format_style (and unit_type where values permit) — any combination.

3. dd_data_unit → unit_type

Rename dd_data_unit to unit_type and move it to sit after format_label/format_style in the column order. Today it holds a menu of possible units (measurement → unit-specific (kg;;m;;C;;L)); under the new model it becomes the resolved (or candidate) value of the unit axis. This is one concept, not two — the rename and the format_label split land together, or we end up with two “unit” fields. The temperature case is the payoff: unit_type of C with a defined convert_C_F and a desired_default_format/target unit of F gives a real, declarable unit transform.

4. New ontology columns (datagoodr asks 3 & 4)

  • replace format_label with format_style + unit_type (unit_type from the renamed dd_data_unit).
  • stable_format → examples only; move any verb token out of it.
  • add desired_default_format — the write_* target to pre-fill when the human expresses no preference (yyyymmdd for calendar, numeric for a USD amount). For units, the default target unit lives here too (e.g. keep C, or a project default of F).
  • carry read_*/write_* tokens in a format DSL with prefix discipline (fx: token · strp: R format · re: regex) and :: reserved for compose (datagoodr ask 6).

5. Migration surface (why this is v7, not an edit)

Touches: the 96 ontology rows + variant_id scheme; R/14-fx-ontology.R (fx_validate_ontology axis checks); the router (format_label is a training label/feature); the verifier and $route builder (R/02-01-guess-data-type.R); fx_stabilize()’s lookup key (currently semantic_type + format_label); the Sherlock/GitTables crosswalk; and datagoodr’s governance mapping. Sequence:

  1. v7 schema — add format_style + unit_type (+ desired_default_format), backfill from today’s format_label/dd_data_unit, keep format_label as a derived convenience for one release.
  2. write_* renderers for the high-frequency styles, then compose read_* :: write_* behind fx_stabilize(..., target_format=).
  3. convert_* registry, starting with temperature and fiscal/calendar year.
  4. detector resolves format_style (and unit_type where value-detectable) as the depth-4 step; router/verifier retrained on the new label axis.

5a. Transformability as a path search (prototyped)

With input and output both expressed as a format (semantic_type, unit_type, format_style), stabilizing a column is a graph search: is there a path from the input format to the desired one through the registry of read_/write_/convert_ edges? A path exists only “if you can get there from here” — a unit change needs a registered convert_*, so the search answers the transformability question instead of assuming it.

Nodes are value states; edges are the three operations:

written(style_a) --read_a-->  canonical(unit_a) --convert_a_b--> canonical(unit_b) --write_b--> written(style_b)

R/22-fx-transform-path.R implements this as a first, additive increment (not yet wired into guess_data_type()/fx_stabilize()):

  • fx_format(semantic_type, format_style, unit_type) — a format descriptor.
  • fx_plan_transform(from, to) — breadth-first search of fx_transforms() for the shortest read :: [convert] :: write composition; returns an fx_plan marked transformable with the path, or not-transformable with a reason.
  • fx_transformable(from, to) / fx_apply_plan(x, plan).

The seeded registry demonstrates the three cases: temperature celsius → C → (convert_C_F) → F → fahrenheit resolves; a calendar reformat with no unit change resolves; and fiscal-year → calendar-year is reported unreachable because convert_fiscal_calendar (which needs the fiscal-year-end convention) is deliberately not registered. v7 grows this registry by generating read_/ write_ edges from each ontology row’s format_style and registering convert_ edges per unit_type pair as they are defined.

Status (2026-10-26)

Done and shipped on main:

  • Schema — format_style, unit_type (renamed from dd_data_unit), desired_default_format added; format_label kept derived. Validation clean.
  • Planner — fx_format / fx_plan_transform / fx_transformable / fx_apply_plan, with canonical endpoints.
  • Registry — generated from the ontology (a read_<style> edge per row) and merged with the hand-authored write_/convert_ seed.
  • Stabilizer — fx_stabilize(..., target_format=) renders via the planner; $route carries format_style.
  • Detectors — day_of_week / month_of_year wired with selective as_dow / as_moy; first_name / quarter / domain reconciled. 41/96 implemented.

Since shipped: the disambiguator (a disambiguator / collision_group column + a cardinality tie-break in the verifier, resolving the geographic and place↔︎geographic collisions, guarded by fx_validate_ontology()); a conversion_log + warning on fx_stabilize() for dropped values; a named-color leaf (text/color/color_name + is_color_name()); and a write_numeric edge so plain numbers stabilize to numeric; and a tags detector (is_tags / as_tags) for delimited list columns. Coverage 48/97.

The migration and the new API surface are complete. Deferred (next release, each its own effort):

  • Router retrain — not needed now (the router trains on format_label, which is retained); required only when format_label is finally removed.
  • Broad write_ renderers — the registry’s write side is still mostly a seed (write_numeric and the calendar/temperature styles exist); grow it so target_format works for more styles.
  • True multi-style detection — $route carries the resolved variant’s format_style; sniffing a column to choose among several styles within one semantic_type (mdy vs dmy vs ymd) is a detector enhancement.
  • convert_ edges per unit pair — temperature done; fiscal/calendar year needs the fiscal-year-end convention from datagoodr. (The currency-amount detector is done — usd / is_currency_amount.) (The tags detector is now done — is_tags / as_tags wire categorical/multiselect/tags.)

6. Does separating add clarity? — verdict

Yes. It removes a redundancy that affects most of the ontology, turns an enumerated leaf set into a compositional space the detector can resolve one axis at a time, and — most importantly — separates the three operations (detect / render / convert) so that user-controllable output and genuine unit conversions (temperature, currency) each have a home. The cost is a real v7 migration, and the one caveat is to keep unit_type for true units (not date field-order) so “resolve the unit” means the same thing in every family.
